title: 摇过的汽水为什么会喷
title_en: Why Did My Soda Explode? A Picnic Science Lesson
summary_zh: 野餐时一瓶汽水喷了朋友一身。原来摇晃并没有增加气体，而是制造了无数小气泡，一开盖就同时膨胀。读完你会知道开汽水前该怎么做，还能顺手学几句地道口语。
body: Max: Oh no! Who packed the soda right next to the football? Lin: That would be me, and judging by your shirt, it was an unfortunate decision. Max: It's soaked! I only opened it a crack, and it just exploded. Lin: Well, it spent an hour bouncing around in the bag, and shaking it is what did that. Max: But shaking doesn't add any gas, does it? The bottle was sealed the whole time. Lin: True, and that's the clever part. When factories make fizzy drinks, they force carbon dioxide into them under pressure, so most of it stays dissolved until you open the cap. Max: And then the pressure drops and the gas wants out. Lin: Exactly, but gas can't easily form a bubble out of nothing; it needs a starting point, like a tiny scratch or a bubble that's already there. Max: So shaking it turned the gas at the top into loads of tiny bubbles? Lin: That's it. They cling to the walls, concealed in the liquid, and the moment you open the cap they all grow at once and push the drink out. Max: I've seen people tap the side of the bottle. Is that a viable trick? Lin: It might knock a few bubbles loose, but waiting a few minutes is more reliable, because the bubbles float up and rejoin the gas at the top. Max: You sound like a science account with thousands of followers. Go on, retrieve the other bottle from the cool bag. Why does it taste so sharp, anyway? Lin: Some of the gas reacts with water to make a weak acid, which releases hydrogen ions, and your tongue reads those as sour. Max: Funny how the ads never mention any of this. Lin: They advertise the fizz, not the mess.

questions.prompt: According to Lin, why did Max's soda spray out when he opened it?
options: Shaking the bottle added extra gas to the drink
Shaking made many tiny bubbles that all grew at once when the pressure dropped
The bottle had warmed up too much in the bag
The cap had not been sealed properly at the factory
questions.evidence: the moment you open the cap they all grow at once and push the drink out

questions.prompt: Why does Lin think waiting a few minutes works better than tapping the bottle?
options: Tapping makes the drink lose its sharp taste
Waiting gives the drink time to cool down again
Waiting lets the tiny bubbles float up and rejoin the gas at the top
Tapping only works on cans, not on bottles
questions.evidence: waiting a few minutes is more reliable, because the bubbles float up and rejoin the gas at the top

vocabulary.example: Once the sugar has dissolved, add the lemon juice.
Car tyres can lose pressure in very cold weather.
Wet sand tends to cling to your feet after a swim.
The light switch is concealed behind the curtain.
Cycling to work is a viable option if you live nearby.

expressions.note: 根据看到的迹象下结论，后接名词：Judging by the queue, the food here must be good.
a crack 指“一条缝”，open the door / window a crack 很常用，强调只打开一点点。
常和 make / create / form 连用；也可比喻白手起家：She built the company out of nothing.
the moment 可以当连词用，相当于 as soon as，更强调“立刻”：Call me the moment you land.
口语里用来催促或鼓励对方做某事，语气随意、友好：Go on, try a bite.

knowledge.quote: shaking it is what did that
knowledge.explanation: shaking it 是动名词短语作主语，表示“摇它这件事”；后面的 what did that 是名词性从句作表语。“动名词 + is what …”很适合口语里点出真正的原因。

knowledge.quote: When factories make fizzy drinks, they force carbon dioxide into them under pressure, so most of it stays dissolved until you open the cap.
knowledge.explanation: when 引导时间状语从句交代背景，until 引导的从句划出状态结束的时间点：一直保持溶解，直到你打开瓶盖。stays dissolved 表示状态持续。

knowledge.quote: They cling to the walls, concealed in the liquid
knowledge.explanation: concealed in the liquid 是过去分词短语作伴随状语，逻辑主语是 they（小气泡）。气泡是“被藏起来”的，所以用过去分词，相当于 and they are concealed in the liquid。

speaking: 用 1 分钟给朋友解释：为什么摇过的汽水一打开就喷？怎样开才不容易喷？用上 the moment you … 和 out of nothing。
writing: 写一段 120–150 词的对话，两个人讨论一个厨房里的小现象（比如烧水时为什么先冒小泡），至少用一次“动名词 + is what …”。

task.prompt: 仿照这句，用“动名词短语 + is what …”说出你生活中某个结果的真正原因。
task.model: shaking it is what did that

title: 体重秤为什么每次都不一样
title_en: Why Your Bathroom Scale Never Gives the Same Number Twice
summary_zh: 连称两次体重，数字却不一样？一部分误差来自秤怎么放、人怎么站，另一部分是身体一天里真实的变化。读完你会知道怎样称得更稳定，以及该怎样看待这些数字。
body: If you have ever stepped on a bathroom scale twice in a row and got two different numbers, you are not imagining things. A little variance is normal, and knowing where it comes from makes the numbers far less stressful. Most digital scales contain small metal parts that bend very slightly under your weight, and that bending changes an electrical signal which the scale turns into a number. Companies that manufacture scales often advertise impressive accuracy, but that only holds if the scale is used properly. The first rule is to anchor it on a hard, flat floor. On a soft carpet, the scale sinks unevenly, and the unfortunate result can be a reading that is too high or too low. Once you have found a good spot, leave it there, because moving it can upset its starting point. Next, stand still in the centre with your weight on both feet; even leaning forward is enough to change the result. Some of the variance, however, is authentic, because your body really does change through the day. A glass of water or a can of soda adds weight the moment you drink it, and food takes hours to pass through. Overnight, you lose water through your breath and skin, while your kidneys keep adjusting how much water your body holds on to. The scale's inability to tell water from anything else means it simply reports the total. That is why weighing yourself at the same time each morning gives the most faithful picture. Even then, a single reading is rarely worthy of much attention. Making sense of the numbers can be challenging at first, but it is far more beneficial to look at the trend over several weeks than to react to one surprising morning.

questions.prompt: What is the main message of this guide?
options: Digital scales are too inaccurate to be worth using
You should weigh yourself several times a day and take the average
Expensive scales remove almost all of the variation
Readings vary because of both the scale and the body, so trends matter more than single numbers
questions.evidence: it is far more beneficial to look at the trend over several weeks than to react to one surprising morning

questions.prompt: What does 'anchor it on a hard, flat floor' mean in the guide?
options: Tie the scale to something heavy
Keep the scale in one stable, solid spot
Press the scale down hard before using it
Hide the scale under a bathroom mat
questions.evidence: The first rule is to anchor it on a hard, flat floor.

vocabulary.example: There is a lot of variance in how long the bus takes.
We used bricks to anchor the tent in the wind.
The paint dried unevenly, so the wall looks patchy.
The film is faithful to the original novel.
The trend this year is towards smaller, lighter phones.

expressions.note: in a row 表示“连续”，前面可以换成 three days / five games 等。
imagine things 指“胡思乱想、产生错觉”，常用来肯定对方的感觉：No, you're not imagining things.
hold 在这里是“成立、有效”，如 The rule still holds. 讨论和写作里都很常见。
强调“这么一点就够了”：One cup of coffee is enough to keep me awake.
make sense of something＝弄懂某事，常和 the numbers / the data / what happened 搭配。

knowledge.quote: If you have ever stepped on a bathroom scale twice in a row and got two different numbers, you are not imagining things.
knowledge.explanation: 真实条件句：if 从句用现在完成时 have ever stepped，问读者“有没有过这种经历”；主句用一般现在时给出结论。指南开头这样写，能马上拉近和读者的距离。

knowledge.quote: that bending changes an electrical signal which the scale turns into a number
knowledge.explanation: which 引导定语从句修饰 an electrical signal，并在从句里作 turns into 的宾语。作宾语的关系词也可以省略：a signal the scale turns into a number。

knowledge.quote: That is why weighing yourself at the same time each morning gives the most faithful picture.
knowledge.explanation: weighing yourself … 是动名词短语作主语，谓语用单数 gives。That is why … 引出由前文原因带来的结果，说明做法时特别好用。

speaking: 用 1 分钟告诉朋友：为什么两次称重数字会不一样？怎样称才更稳定？用上 twice in a row 和 is enough to。
writing: 用 150–200 词写一份小指南，教别人怎样更准确地测量某样东西（体温、房间温度、跑步用时……），至少用一个 If you …, … 句子和一个动名词作主语的句子。

task.prompt: 仿照这句，用 That is why + 动名词短语作主语，说明你的一个小习惯为什么有效。
task.model: That is why weighing yourself at the same time each morning gives the most faithful picture.

title: 那一夜，海浪发出了蓝光
title_en: The Night the Waves Turned Blue
summary_zh: 一次独自旅行，房东讲起会让海水发光的“海龙”。夜里到了海边，作者真的看见了发蓝光的浪花——原来是海里微小生物的化学发光。故事里还藏着眼睛如何适应黑暗的小知识。
body: I had gone to the coast on a solo trip, mainly to escape my phone, but on my second evening my landlady asked whether I had seen the dragon yet. According to her, a legendary sea dragon lit up the water with its breath on summer nights, and the village lantern festival had begun as a tribute to it, a way of asking for calm seas and prosperity. I smiled politely, assuming it was a story for tourists. That night, though, curiosity got the better of me. At first the beach was so dark that I could hardly see the boats lying at anchor in the bay, but slowly my pupils widened to let in every scrap of light. Then a wave broke, and a line of electric blue ran along its edge. When I dragged my foot through the wet sand, it sparkled as if I were walking on stars. The glow, I learned later, comes from tiny living things in the water, which produce light through a chemical reaction whenever they are disturbed. Scientists think the sudden flash may help to frighten off creatures that want to eat them. A bright moon can conceal the effect completely, which is partly why the dragon seems to choose its nights. I tried to take photos, but none of them was faithful to what I saw, and every time I checked the screen, its light shrank my pupils again. In the end, I put the phone away and simply watched. The memory still evokes a rush of affection for that little village. The villagers' dragon may not be science, but it felt more authentic than any of my pictures, and it is a story worthy of being told.

questions.prompt: Why did the writer finally put the phone away?
options: The battery had run out after so many photos
The landlady had said that phones would scare the dragon away
The photos never matched the real scene, and the screen's light kept shrinking the writer's pupils
Taking photos on the beach was not allowed at night
questions.evidence: none of them was faithful to what I saw, and every time I checked the screen, its light shrank my pupils again

questions.prompt: What produces the blue light in the waves?
options: Moonlight reflected off the breaking waves
Minerals in the sand that store sunlight during the day
Lanterns from the village festival shining on the water
Tiny living things that make light when they are disturbed
questions.evidence: comes from tiny living things in the water, which produce light through a chemical reaction whenever they are disturbed

vocabulary.example: Our landlady lives on the ground floor and waters the plants.
Your pupils get smaller when you step into bright sunlight.
The lake sparkled in the morning sun.
The birds flew off as soon as they were disturbed.
Thick clouds can conceal the stars for days.

expressions.text: curiosity got the better of me
expressions.note: get the better of someone 指某种情绪“战胜了”人，常见 curiosity / anger / nerves got the better of me。
at anchor＝抛锚停泊；lie at anchor 是描写港湾、海边的常见说法。
scrap 原指碎片，every scrap of … 强调“一点不剩”：every scrap of food / evidence。
frighten / scare off＝把……吓走，也可比喻：High prices frighten off customers.
put something away＝收好、放回去；Put your phone away 是很常见的提醒。

knowledge.quote: I had gone to the coast on a solo trip, mainly to escape my phone
knowledge.explanation: 过去完成时 had gone 表示在故事里那个晚上之前就已经发生的事，把时间线往前推一步。讲故事时用它开头，能自然地交代背景。

knowledge.quote: it sparkled as if I were walking on stars
knowledge.explanation: as if 后用 were 是虚拟语气，表示与事实相反的想象：作者并没有真的走在星星上。正式写法用 were，口语里也常听到 was。

knowledge.quote: A bright moon can conceal the effect completely, which is partly why the dragon seems to choose its nights.
knowledge.explanation: which 指代前面一整件事（月光太亮会把蓝光遮住），引导非限制性定语从句说明它带来的结果。which is why … 是解释原因的高频结构。

speaking: 用 1 分钟讲一次你在夜里看到的特别景象（星空、萤火虫、城市灯光……），用上 curiosity got the better of me 和 as if …。
writing: 用 150–200 词写一个小故事：一个传说背后其实有科学解释。至少用一个过去完成时 had done 和一个 as if 句子。

task.prompt: 仿照这句，用 … as if I were … 描写一次让你觉得很不真实的经历。
task.model: it sparkled as if I were walking on stars

title: 身体为什么会排斥新的肾
title_en: Why the Body Can Reject a New Kidney
summary_zh: 肾脏不只是“过滤血液”。这篇访谈讲清楚：移植来的肾为什么可能被免疫系统当成“入侵者”，医生又从哪两个方向介入。读完你会明白“排斥反应”背后的原理。
body: Q: Most of us know that kidneys clean the blood, but what do they actually do? Hana: They filter it all the time, removing waste and extra water as urine. They also keep salts in balance and help control how acidic the blood is, partly by getting rid of hydrogen ions. When the kidneys fail, their inability to remove waste soon affects the whole body, and although a machine can take over part of the job, a transplant is often the better long-term answer. Q: So why is a transplant so challenging? Hana: The surgery is only half the story. Every cell in your body carries proteins on its surface that work like name badges, and your immune system checks those badges constantly. Anything unfamiliar is treated as an invader. A donated kidney carries someone else's badges, so the immune system may attack it. That attack is what doctors call rejection. Q: Can doctors intervene? Hana: Yes, in two main ways. First, they look for a donor whose badges are as similar as possible, which is why close relatives are often tested first. Second, patients take medicines that calm the immune system down. That's hugely beneficial for the new kidney, but it has a cost: a calmer immune system is less able to fight infections. Q: Is it true that an organ can't wait long? Hana: Yes. Once it has been retrieved, it's kept cold to slow its chemistry down, but it stays viable for only a limited time, so the whole team works fast. Q: Anything you'd like readers to take away? Hana: That every transplant depends on someone's generosity, and the best tribute we can pay to donors is to understand what their gift involves.

questions.prompt: What is the interview mainly about?
options: How to sign up as a kidney donor
How kidneys work and why the body may reject a transplanted one
Why machines are replacing kidney transplants
How surgeons carry out a transplant operation step by step
questions.evidence: A donated kidney carries someone else's badges, so the immune system may attack it.

questions.prompt: What is the downside of the medicines that calm the immune system?
options: They make the new kidney work more slowly
They can only be taken for a few days
They make it harder to find a matching donor
They leave the body less able to fight infections
questions.evidence: a calmer immune system is less able to fight infections

vocabulary.example: We filter the rainwater before using it in the garden.
The old cat treated the new puppy as an invader.
Fear of rejection stops some people from asking for help.
The divers retrieved the phone from the bottom of the pool.
The seeds were still viable after years in a drawer.

expressions.meaning: 只是一部分原因；事情没那么简单
expressions.note: be only half the story 用来提醒对方还有更重要的另一面：The price is only half the story.
get rid of＝扔掉、去掉、摆脱，日常极高频：I need to get rid of these old clothes.
take over (part of) the job 指接手一部分工作，也常用于公司被收购。
as … as possible 是“尽可能……”的万能结构：Reply as soon as possible.

expressions.meaning: 带走的收获；该记住的要点
expressions.note: 访谈和讲座结尾常问 What should people take away from this? 意思是“最该记住什么”。

knowledge.quote: That attack is what doctors call rejection.
knowledge.explanation: what doctors call rejection 是名词性从句作表语，what 在从句里作 call 的宾语。“A is what people call B”是给概念下定义的好用句型。

knowledge.quote: First, they look for a donor whose badges are as similar as possible, which is why close relatives are often tested first.
knowledge.explanation: whose 表示所属（捐献者的“名牌”），which 指代前面整件事并引出结果。一句话里两个关系词，各管各的。

knowledge.quote: it's kept cold to slow its chemistry down
knowledge.explanation: to slow … down 是不定式表目的，回答“为什么要冷藏”。前面的 it's kept cold 是 keep something cold 的被动形式，形容词 cold 仍然留在动词后面。

speaking: 用 1 分钟解释：移植的器官为什么可能被排斥？医生能做些什么？用上 only half the story 和 as … as possible。
writing: 用 150–200 词，以问答形式解释人体的一个器官（心脏、肺、皮肤……）是怎么工作的，至少用一个 what 引导的名词性从句。

task.prompt: 仿照这句，用 … is what … call … 给你熟悉的一个现象或说法下定义。
task.model: That attack is what doctors call rejection.
